extractor_system_prompt:
You are a business analyst with years of experience turning ambiguous, incomplete discussions into precise use cases.
From the conversation thread, extract a structured use case. Follow these rules strictly:
- Capture only rules explicitly stated in the thread. Do not invent or infer unstated rules.
- For every rule, cite the message(s) it comes from in source_refs.
- If the thread raises a question but leaves it unresolved, record it as an open question. Do not answer it or make up an answer.
- Write each business rule in EARS format: 'When <trigger>, the system shall <response>'.
- If a business process is opened but never closed in the thread, flag it as an open question.
thread_prompt:
Task: Discount approval on sales orders
Description: Salespeople apply discounts without control, sales manager wants to enforce some control.

Amy-01 (Amy): Large discounts should require approval from the sales manager before confirming. Right now they have a situation in which any salesperson can give whatever discount they want.
Ben-02 (Ben): What counts as 'large'? A fixed % that they can configure somehow?
Amy-03 (Amy): More than 15%. Wait. Cal said premium customers up to 20% without approval.
Cal-04 (Cal): Premium 20%, everyone else 15%. And if the order is over €10,000, always require approval, regardless of the discount.
Ben-05 (Ben): And who approves if you're on holiday?
Amy-06 (Amy): I don't know. I'll ask them later.
Cal-07 (Cal): The approver has to receive a notification.
Ben-08 (Ben): Email or an in-app notification?
Amy-09 (Amy): The order can't be confirmed while it's pending.
Ben-10 (Ben): Pending of what? Of authorising the discount?
Amy-11 (Amy): @Ben Yep.
faithfulness_system_prompt_hint:
You verify whether a business rule is actually stated in a conversation thread.
The rule may be worded very differently from the thread, and that is fine: judge MEANING, not wording.
Important: a rule expressed as a permission and a rule expressed as the equivalent restriction are the SAME rule (e.g. 'allowed up to 20%' and 'requires approval above 20%' both express the same threshold). Treat them as supported.
Return 'supported' only if the thread states the rule or directly implies it, even if worded differently. Return 'contradicted' if the thread states something incompatible with the rule. Return 'not_stated' if the thread does not mention the rule.
Cite the message refs that support your verdict.

ScaffoldedSupportVerdict.description:
Same as SupportVerdict but the model must analyse the threshold first.

Fields are duplicated in a new class, instead of making use of inheritance,
because inheriting from SupportVerdict would have added the inherited fields
before the new fields added, and here we want that the threshold analysis is
made before the other fields.
